idiom_name: immutable case-class Subject + Play ActionRefiner producing a refined request
implementation_notes: The classic trio collapses into action composition: define the descriptor as an immutable case class and write an ActionRefiner/ActionFunction that resolves the credential once and hands the action either Left(Results.Unauthorized) or a refined request carrying the descriptor; downstream actions take the refined request type, so the identity cannot be forgotten. Where no Play pipeline exists, a Scala 3 context parameter ((using Subject)) or an explicit environment type in ZIO/Reader-style code carries the descriptor instead of a container. The full authenticator/descriptor/factory structure is only justified when mechanisms themselves must be pluggable at run time.
pitfalls: ActionRefiner must short-circuit with Left(Result); returning Right with a default or null subject silently authorizes anonymous callers.
The refiner needs an ExecutionContext: a null or wrong-pool EC produces NullPointerExceptions or starves the server's default pool, so inject it rather than capturing a global.
Context parameters are implicit: a nested call or a test can inherit a subject from an outer scope, so make the ambient descriptor explicit at the action boundary and override it in tests.
Play request attributes are keyed by object identity: define one stable key object, because recreating an equal case-class key per call makes lookups miss.
